title: Learning to Inhabit Your Body: Yoga
coreMove: Trauma-sensitive body practice helps when it makes sensation voluntary, tolerable, and useful, so regulation can return before traumatic memory is pushed.

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician whose body stays activated after a crisis
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next call may arrive before arousal has settled
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show breath and voluntary movement as a brief regulation practice

exampleSpecs.audience: a facilitator replacing performance cues with consent cues
exampleSpecs.stakes: ordinary studio language may turn practice into pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show adapted yoga inviting choice before effort

exampleSpecs.audience: an analyst summarizing a trauma program
exampleSpecs.stakes: a good number can become an overclaim if the method disappears
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use HRV and PTSD data without turning yoga into a cure claim

exampleSpecs.audience: a counselor deciding where care should begin
exampleSpecs.stakes: starting too fast may turn help into exposure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: place body awareness before traumatic memory narration

exampleSpecs.audience: a worker tracking pain without self-blame
exampleSpecs.stakes: chronic arousal can hide inside normal deadlines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show body symptoms becoming useful signals

exampleSpecs.audience: an attorney choosing language for a trauma referral
exampleSpecs.stakes: a cure promise may make support feel coercive
